newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bratislava BSE hits yr-high on blue chip gains.
newsitem.headline: Bratislava BSE hits yr-high on blue chip gains.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in heavier trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with gains to several blue chips boosting the SAX index 0.41 points to a year-high of 202.62.

Brokers said the growth potential in most of the heavily- weighted issues, boosted by continued demand, should help the bourse extend its upward trend over the week, though they warned there could be a slight correction next week.
Steel producer VSZ led trading on the BSE floor closing up eight crowns at 706 with 31,824 shares changing hands.

"Today's trades with VSZ appear to have been a set of three larger packages of an agreed deal settled through the bourse, and, in this case, the price does not neccessarilly reflect market value," said Jan Laluha of CSOB Bank.
But he added that, given the company's expected good 1996 results, the share had potential to increase even further.
VUB bank rose 34 crowns, or 1.98 percent, to 1,750 crowns, and dealers said that continued demand and low liquidity could boost its price higher in the near future.
"There is continuing demand for several blue chips, such as VUB or Slovnaft, but they remain iliquid, which could boost their prices in coming days," Laluha said.

The best-performing share on the unlisted market over the past few weeks, drug maker Slovakofarma, fell 100 crowns to 5,100, and brokers said waning foreign demand could steady its price at current levels for sometime.

"We will probably have to wait for some time until there is a larger package to sell available, and this could again push the Slovakofarma's price up, as it was also the case with its rally over the past month," said Laluha.
Overall volume rose to 774,064 shares, from 421,571 shares traded on Friday, while turnover fell to 472.45 million crowns, from 623.15 million.
